clue.text: Scaling rocks when visiting favourite Hebridean location

indicators.note: one piece visiting another goes to stay inside it, so the jumbled letters sit within the other piece

parts.note: fave is an informal word for a favourite

indicators.note: something that rocks is shaken about, so the letters of scaling are jumbled

explanation.surface: A climber scales the cliffs on a trip to a beloved spot in the Hebrides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like the cliffs being climbed, but it is the anagram signal; 'when visiting' sends the jumble inside the informal word for favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingal's Cave is a famous sea cave on the island of Staffa in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland.

clue.text: Instigates Times leader being changed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: moments are times, points in time

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial is altered, stirring up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' reads as the newspaper's editorial; in fact 'Times' is MOMENTS and its leader M becomes F.
explanation.definitionFit: To foment trouble is to stir it up, so foments is a synonym of instigates.

clue.text: Subtlety of problem is overlooked

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: a nuisance is a problem or bother

explanation.surface: A fine point of a difficulty gets missed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a slight shade of meaning, a subtle distinction.

clue.text: Male fragrance Eva's father ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: Eva's dad has bought himself some cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like buying; it is the anagram signal on EVAS FATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a scented lotion men put on after shaving, a typical men's scent.

clue.text: Small storage facility in Slough

definitions.meaning: a small hut for storing tools and the like
to slough is to cast off skin

explanation.surface: A little garden hut in the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, so 'in Slough' looks like a location; here slough is the verb meaning cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a garden hut for tools, and casting off an outer layer like skin.

clue.text: Worry about Republican that is becoming most incensed

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the others, enclosing them

parts.note: angst is anxiety or worry

explanation.surface: Fretting about a Republican makes someone more and more furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Angriest is the superlative of angry; someone incensed is enraged, so most incensed is angriest.

clue.text: Watch dance in which pupil's seen?

parts.note: the pupil is the dark centre of the eye
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on a school dance where a student might be spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' suggests a schoolchild at the dance; it is the part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at or look hard at them, so to watch.

clue.text: Agreement is close

explanation.surface: A deal is nearly done.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact as noun is a pact or treaty; as adjective it means tightly packed together.

clue.text: Claim Tommy is occasionally permitted each drink

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then means every other letter of these words

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Tommy says he is sometimes allowed a drink of his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Camomile tea is a herbal infusion made from camomile flowers, a soothing beverage.

clue.text: Intellectual for instance claims golf title

indicators.note: the outer pieces claim, or take in, the letter between them

parts.note: a head or heading is a title at the top of a page
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A brainy person claims a golfing championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'title' suggests a sporting championship; it is a heading.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal word for a highbrow, bookish person.

clue.text: Disheartened daughter supports protest Israel condemned

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports others sits beneath them, at the end

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked, so the letters of Israel are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dejected girl backs a demonstration denouncing Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' turns ISRAEL into RALISE; D goes under it as 'supports' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoralised means having lost confidence or hope, which is being disheartened.

clue.text: Dress restricts one about to get beauty treatment

indicators.note: the outer word restricts, or hems in, the letters placed inside it

parts.note: to dress soil is to manure it
I is the Roman numeral for one
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A frock that confines someone about to have their nails done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like clothing; gardeners dress land with manure.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is a cosmetic treatment of the hands and nails.

clue.text: Placate retired gentleman when ill-tempered on vacation

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: Mr is the title of a gentleman
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Calming a grumpy pensioner while he is away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties ill-tempered to ID; the whole MRASID is read backwards, as 'retired' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to win them over and remove their hostility, so to placate them.

clue.text: Bravery investing fortune in conifer plantations ultimately succeeded

indicators.note: to invest is to surround or besiege, so the pines enclose the luck

parts.note: pines are conifers; the plural stands for stands of them
luck is fortune
s is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees; ultimately says it comes in at the end

explanation.surface: A brave move: sinking a fortune into forestry finally pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' reads as finance; here it means surrounding. 'ultimately' just says the S for succeeded comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluckiness is the quality of having pluck, meaning courage or spirit.

clue.text: Essential new wine

definitions.meaning: a ... is something essential, as in 'a ...-see'
unfermented grape juice, wine in the making

explanation.surface: A young vintage is not to be missed.
explanation.definitionFit: A must is a necessity; must is also freshly pressed grape juice before fermentation.

clue.text: One supplying retailer with pickle and salt, reportedly

parts.note: a hole is a fix or pickle, a tricky situation

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is heard rather than read, matching by sound

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor; said aloud the word matches the last letters of the answer

explanation.surface: A trader brings a shopkeeper chutney and salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle and salt' look like groceries: a pickle is a fix, a hole, and an old salt is a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler sells goods in bulk to shops, which then sell them on to the public.

clue.text: Curious new difficulty upset poet

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: nosy means inquisitive, curious
a net is a snare, a trap that lands one in difficulty

explanation.surface: An odd new problem has distressed a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' looks like the anagram signal; it is NOSY, and 'upset' reverses NOSY N NET.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Poet Laureate for much of Queen Victoria's reign.

clue.text: Army, perhaps on edge, professed loyalty that's insincere

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a lip is a rim or edge
the army is an example of one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A jittery soldier swears allegiance he does not feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' reads as nervous, but it splits: 'on' is the positional link and 'edge' is the rim of a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip service is support expressed in words but not backed by action.

clue.text: Present hairstyle, cut by pro

indicators.note: the outer word is cut into by the other piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: a perm is a hairstyle with lasting curls
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A professional stylist gives someone a new hairdo as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is the verb, to put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To present a play or piece of music is to perform it.

clue.text: Setter maybe signifies contentment with this indicator?

definitions.text: Setter maybe signifies contentment with this indicator?

parts.words: Setter maybe signifies contentment with this indicator
parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, and a dog wags this to show it is happy

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler shows pleasure through a clue signal.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'setter' and 'indicator' mean the compiler and a clue signal; here the setter is a gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's wagging rear appendage works as a signal, or indicator, of its mood.

clue.text: To some extent sweetheart is a natural craftsperson

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lover is partly a born talent.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker who makes things by hand.

clue.text: Cloak on cop ruined, husband's admitted

indicators.note: the letter is let in, placed inside the scrambled letters
something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A policeman's cape is spoiled once a husband is let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns ON COP into PONCO, and 'admitted' puts H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a blanket-like cloak with a slit for the head.

clue.text: Arduous round trip regularly ignored before

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second
skipping letters at regular intervals leaves every other letter of the word

parts.note: a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: A tough journey there and back, often overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiring wears a person out, so it is arduous or exhausting.

clue.text: Retorts from priest so unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters take a different, odd arrangement

explanation.surface: Sharp comebacks from a cleric who is odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, clever reply, a retort.

clue.text: Side with upper hand

definitions.meaning: a side or border of something
having the ... means having the advantage

explanation.surface: Taking sides gives one an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a border or side, and also an advantage over a rival.

clue.text: Partied, leaving clubs excited

indicators.note: a letter leaving goes away, so it is taken out of the word

parts.note: caroused means drank and made merry, partied
C is clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: Revellers left the nightclubs in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests nightclubs; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Aroused means stirred up or stimulated, roused to excitement.

clue.text: Sought to justify former copper's heartless intent

parts.note: ex means former
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the 's

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: an end is an aim or intent

explanation.surface: A former policeman tried to explain away his cruel intentions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse something is to offer reasons in its defence, attempting to justify it.

clue.text: Homeless vagrant hugs extremely nonplussed northern composer

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hug, or enclose, the other pair
vagrant means wandering, so these letters wander into a new order
extremely means taking the extreme letters, first and last, of the word

explanation.surface: A homeless drifter embraces a bewildered northern musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vagrant' turns HOMELESS into MEELSSOH, which 'hugs' ND from 'extremely nonplussed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix Mendelssohn was a German Romantic composer, famous for the Hebrides Overture.
